title: Another fuel price rollback on November 17
summary: This marks the second straight week of subtantial rollbacks for gasoline, diesel, and kerosene

blocks.text: A gas station in Manila adjusts fuel prices after another round of oil price increases, with partial adjustments already in effect, on March 17, 2026.
This marks the second straight week of subtantial rollbacks for gasoline, diesel, and kerosene
MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices are going down again starting Tuesday, November 17, with diesel and kerosene seeing big drops in particular.
The Department of Energy (DOE) announced the following minimum price decreases for the week of November 17 to 23:

items: Gasoline – rollback of at least P1.50 per liter
Diesel – rollback of at least P3.80 per liter
Kerosene – rollback of at least P5.80 per liter

blocks.text: The adjustments follow last week’s big rollbacks, when gasoline prices went down by P16.80 per liter, followed by diesel at P4.10 and kerosene by P3.70.
The latest reductions as the prospect of a diplomatic solution to the conflict between the US and Iran brought down concerns over global oil supplies.

Still, local pump prices remain substantially higher than before US and Israel attacked on Iran on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, common Metro Manila prices stood at P56 per liter for RON95 gasoline, P54.70 for RON91, P55 for diesel, and P83.47 for kerosene.
The Philippines imports much of its petroleum requirements as finished products, making domestic prices vulnerable to changes in regional fuel markets, freight costs, and foreign exchange rates.

Meanwhile, excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene remain suspended under Executive Order No. 125, issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in September. The relief does not cover gasoline or diesel. – Rappler.com
